version.changelog:
Initial release of the lobster-dev skill for Lobster AI development.

- Provides an in-depth development guide for contributing to the Lobster multi-agent bioinformatics engine.
- Documents key architectural components, agent/service creation, and essential development rules.
- Includes quick navigation to reference docs, common task guides, and code structure overview.
- Defines patterns for agent registration, service building, logging, and testing.
- Offers command-line workflow examples and links to online/local documentation.
- Lists requirements for code organization, reproducibility, and best practices for contributors.

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: lobster-bio-dev
Version: 1.0.0

The OpenClaw AgentSkills skill bundle provides comprehensive development documentation for the Lobster AI platform. All files (SKILL.md, references/*.md) contain guides for creating agents and services, CLI usage, testing, and architectural overviews. There is no evidence of intentional harmful behavior such as data exfiltration, backdoor installation, or unauthorized remote control. The instructions are directed at human developers, and the example commands are standard development and diagnostic steps. No prompt injection attempts against the AI agent were found, and external links are for documentation reference only.

llm.summary: The skill's documentation and runtime instructions match its stated purpose (developer guide for Lobster AI); there are minor inconsistencies around declared environment requirements but nothing that suggests intentional misdirection.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (Lobster development) align with the provided files: developer guides, agent/service patterns, CLI reference, testing guidance and code-layout. All requested artifacts are appropriate for a developer-contribution skill.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md is an instruction-only skill that guides development tasks (make dev-install, pytest, register entry points, create agents/services). It references workspace files and CLI commands and expects the agent/developer to interact with the repository and local workspace. The instructions do not direct reading/transmitting of unrelated system secrets or reach out to unexpected external endpoints beyond normal dev/documentation links, but they are broad (e.g., 'run dev-install', 'lobster query') and will rely on whatever local environment the user/agent runs in.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec and no code files are executed by the registry — the skill is instruction-only, so it does not download or write code to disk during installation. This is the lowest-risk install model.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill manifest declares no required environment variables, but the CLI reference and docs in SKILL.md mention several environment variables (e.g., LOBSTER_WORKSPACE, LOBSTER_MODEL, LOBSTER_PROVIDER, OPENAI_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, AWS_PROFILE). Those variables are reasonable for developing/running the Lobster CLI, but the manifest's lack of declared env expectations is an inconsistency. An agent following these instructions could rely on or access these secrets from the runtime environment, so users should be aware the skill assumes access to LLM and cloud credentials if you follow the CLI/run guidance.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request persistent presence (always: false), does not request config path access in the manifest, and does not modify other skills' configs. It is a normal, user-invocable development helper.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill is a developer guide for the Lobster AI codebase and appears coherent with that purpose. Before installing or running any commands from this skill: 1) Be aware the docs reference LLM and cloud environment variables (OPENAI_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, AWS_PROFILE, etc.) — do not expose secrets you don't intend to share; run in an isolated/dev environment if possible. 2) Review the repository files (packages/, lobster/) referenced by the skill if you will run 'make dev-install' or tests. 3) Verify external links (docs.omics-os.com) and trustworthiness of the source; this package has no homepage and unknown source, so prefer running inside a sandbox/VM or with least-privilege credentials. 4) If you expect this skill to require access to API keys or AWS, consider adding required env vars to the manifest or explicitly confirming which credentials are needed before use.
llm.findings: [no_regex_findings] expected: The static regex scanner found nothing to analyze because this is an instruction-only skill (no code files). That is expected for a documentation/dev-skill; absence of findings does not prove safety.
